title: SIM-CoT: Supervised Implicit Chain-of-Thought
claim: Scaling latent reasoning steps causes training collapse because latent representations lose information and become homogeneous, similar to each other and detached from the vocabulary.
layout: 4 panels in 2x2 grid; line plot, bar chart, distance area plot, text examples
description: A 2x2 grid of panels that diagnoses why implicit chain-of-thought training fails. (a) is a line plot of accuracy against epoch. Short colored segments for 1 to 4 latent tokens rise, then the dashed purple 5-latent curve spikes and crashes to a red-marked low of 12.5%. A blue arrow labeled 'multi-stage training curriculum' runs across the panel. (b) is a grouped bar chart of number, operator and answer accuracy for 1, 2, 4 and 5 latent tokens and a failed model. Operator accuracy falls to 4.7 in the failed model. (c) overlays teal and pink area curves for vocab distance and latent distance. Inset: an orange ellipse containing two red latent dots and a green vocab center. A red curved arrow marks the narrowing. (d) shows a math word problem and two rounded boxes with decoded latent tokens. The normal model decodes varied operators and numbers, and the failed model decodes mostly numbers. Emoji faces mark good and bad.
caption: (a) The latent instability issue: while using more implicit tokens initially improves accuracy, training becomes unstable and sometimes collapses. (b) Information Loss: the implicit tokens of failed models (5 latent tokens) lose crucial information about operators (like +, −), which makes complex reasoning impossible. (c) Shifted Distance: the latent-to-latent distance of failed models shrinks and becomes too similar to each other, while the latent drifts away from the central vocabulary embedding space. (d) Semantic Homogenization: failed models produce similar latent representations, resulting in a narrower range of decoded tokens, mostly numbers, as opposed to the more varied content generated by a normal model.
abstract: Implicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) methods offer a token-efficient alternative to explicit CoT reasoning in Large Language Models (LLMs), but a persistent performance gap has limited their adoption. We identify a core latent instability issue when scaling the computational budget of implicit CoT: as the number of reasoning tokens increases, training often becomes unstable and collapses. Our analysis shows that this instability arises from latent representations becoming homogeneous and losing semantic diversity, caused by insufficient step-level supervision in current implicit CoT methods. To address this, we propose SIM-CoT, a plug-and-play training module that introduces step-level supervision to stabilize and enrich the latent reasoning space. SIM-CoT employs an auxiliary decoder during training to align each implicit token with its corresponding explicit reasoning step, ensuring latent states capture distinct and meaningful information. The auxiliary decoder is removed at inference, preserving the efficiency of implicit CoT with no added overhead. It also provides interpretability by projecting each latent token onto an explicit reasoning vocabulary, enabling per-step visualization and diagnosis. SIM-CoT significantly improves both in-domain accuracy and out-of-domain stability of implicit CoT methods, boosting Coconut by +8.2\% on GPT-2 and CODI by +3.0\% on LLaMA-3.1 8B. It further surpasses the explicit CoT baseline on GPT-2 by 2.1\% with 2.3$\times$ greater token efficiency, while closing the performance gap on larger models like LLaMA-3.1 8B. Code: https://github.com/InternLM/SIM-CoT
